title: IELTS Academic 19 - Listening Test 1 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

15:12ANNOUNCER: Part 3. You will hear two food science students called Marie and Colin discussing their final year projects.
15:21ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
15:47ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
15:55COLIN: I haven't seen you for a bit, Marie.
15:58MARIE: No. I've been busy with my project.
16:01COLIN: You're making a vegan alternative to eggs, aren't you? Something that doesn't use animal products?
16:07MARIE: Yes. I'm using chickpeas. I had two main aims when I first started looking for an alternative to eggs, but actually I've found chickpeas have got more advantages.
16:20COLIN: Right.
16:21MARIE: But how about your project on reusing waste food – you were looking at bread, weren't you?
16:28COLIN: Yes. It's been hard work, but I've enjoyed it. The basic process was quite straightforward – breaking the stale bread down to a paste then reforming it.
16:41MARIE: But you were using 3-D printing, weren't you, to make the paste into biscuits?
16:46COLIN: Yeah, I'd used that before, but in this project, I had time to play around with different patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a more appetising colour, and I was really pleased with what I managed to produce.
17:04MARIE: It must've been a great feeling to make something appetising out of bits of old bread that would've been thrown away otherwise.
17:12COLIN: It was. And I'm hoping that some of the restaurants in town will be interested in the biscuits. I'm going to send them some samples.
17:22MARIE: I came across something on the internet yesterday that might interest you. It was a company that's developed touch-sensitive sensors for food labels. It's a special sort of label on the food package. When the label's smooth, the food is fresh and then when you can feel bumps on the label, that means the food's gone bad. It started off as a project to help visually impaired people know whether food was fit to eat or not.
17:55COLIN: Interesting. So just solid food?
17:58MARIE: No, things like milk and juice as well. But actually, I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and pharmacies.
18:09COLIN: Right. And coming back to food, maybe it'd be possible to use it for other things besides freshness. Like how many kilograms a joint of meat is, for example.
18:19MARIE: Yes, there's all sorts of possibilities.
18:26ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
19:04ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
19:11COLIN: I was reading an article about food trends predicting how eating habits might change in the next few years.
19:19MARIE: Oh – things like more focus on local products? That seems so obvious, but the shops are still full of imported foods.
19:28COLIN: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that. MARIE: And somehow motivate consumers to change, yes.
19:36COLIN: One thing everyone's aware of is the need for a reduction in unnecessary packaging – but just about everything you buy in supermarkets is still covered in plastic. The government needs to do something about it. MARIE: Absolutely. It's got to change.
19:54COLIN: Do you think there'll be more interest in gluten- and lactose-free food?
20:00MARIE: For people with allergies or food intolerances? I don't know. Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now. COLIN: Yes, even if they haven't been diagnosed with an allergy.
20:16MARIE: That's right. One thing I've noticed is the number of branded products related to celebrity chefs – people watch them cooking on TV and then buy things like spice mixes or frozen foods with the chef's name on... I bought something like that once, but I won't again. COLIN: Yeah – I bought a ready-made spice mix... and it didn't actually taste of anything.
20:47MARIE: Mm. Did the article mention 'ghost kitchens' used to produce takeaway food?
20:53COLIN: No. What are they?
20:54MARIE: Well, they might have the name of a restaurant, but actually they're a cooking facility just for delivery meals – the public don't ever go there. But people aren't aware of that – it's all kept very quiet.
21:09COLIN: So people don't realise the food's not actually from the restaurant? Right. Did you know more and more people are using all sorts of different mushrooms now, to treat different health concerns? Things like heart problems?
21:26MARIE: Hmm. They might be taking a big risk there. COLIN: Yes, it's hard to know which varieties are safe to eat. But anyway...
21:42ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3.

groups.title: Questions 21 and 22
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO things did Colin find most satisfying about his bread reuse project?

groups.title: Questions 23 and 24
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO ways do the students agree that touch-sensitive sensors for food labels could be developed in future?

groups.title: Questions 25–30
groups.instructions:
What is the students' opinion about each of the following food trends?
Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 25–30.

options.text: This is only relevant to young people.
This already seems to be widespread.
Retailers should do more to encourage this.
More financial support is needed for this.
Most people know little about this.
There should be stricter regulations about this.

q21.text: Satisfying aspects of bread reuse project (1st choice):
options: A. receiving support from local restaurants
B. finding a good way to prevent waste
C. overcoming problems in a basic process
D. experimenting with designs and colours
E. learning how to apply 3-D printing

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B hoặc D (In either order)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'play around with different patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a more appetising colour' = D (experimenting with designs and colours).
• 'make something appetising out of bits of old bread that would've been thrown away otherwise' = B (finding a good way to prevent waste).

q22.text: Satisfying aspects of bread reuse project (2nd choice):
options: A. receiving support from local restaurants
B. finding a good way to prevent waste
C. overcoming problems in a basic process
D. experimenting with designs and colours
E. learning how to apply 3-D printing

steps: • Đáp án đúng: D hoặc B (In either order)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: Xem giải thích chi tiết ở Câu 21.

q23.text: Future applications of touch-sensitive sensors (1st choice):
options: A. for use on medical products
B. to show that food is no longer fit to eat
C. for use with drinks as well as foods
D. to provide applications for blind people
E. to indicate the weight of certain foods

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A hoặc E (In either order)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and pharmacies.' -> A (for use on medical products).
• 'use it for other things besides freshness. Like how many kilograms a joint of meat is' -> E (to indicate the weight of certain foods).

q24.text: Future applications of touch-sensitive sensors (2nd choice):
options: A. for use on medical products
B. to show that food is no longer fit to eat
C. for use with drinks as well as foods
D. to provide applications for blind people
E. to indicate the weight of certain foods

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E hoặc A (In either order)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: Xem giải thích chi tiết ở Câu 23.
• Đáp án đúng: D (Retailers should do more to encourage this)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'shops are still full of imported foods. COLIN: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that. MARIE: And somehow motivate consumers to change'.
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'shops need to be more proactive... motivate consumers' = Retailers should do more to encourage this.
• Đáp án đúng: G (There should be stricter regulations about this)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'supermarkets is still covered in plastic. The government needs to do something about it. MARIE: Absolutely. It's got to change.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'The government needs to do something' = stricter regulations.
• Đáp án đúng: C (This already seems to be widespread)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now. COLIN: Yes, even if they haven't been diagnosed with an allergy.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'Lots of people... for years now' = already seems to be widespread.

q28.text: Use of branded products related to celebrity chefs

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (This may have disappointing results)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I bought something like that once, but I won't again. COLIN: Yeah – I bought a ready-made spice mix... and it didn't actually taste of anything.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'didn't actually taste of anything / won't buy again' = disappointing results.

q29.text: Development of 'ghost kitchens' for takeaway food

steps: • Đáp án đúng: F (Most people know little about this)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'the public don't ever go there. But people aren't aware of that – it's all kept very quiet. COLIN: So people don't realise...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'people aren't aware of that / don't realise' = know little about this.

q30.text: Use of mushrooms for common health concerns

steps: • Đáp án đúng: H (This could be dangerous)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'They might be taking a big risk there. COLIN: Yes, it's hard to know which varieties are safe to eat.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'taking a big risk / hard to know which are safe' = could be dangerous.
